questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is true about Krebs cycle?

options.text: It is the final common pathway for the oxidation of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins
Pyruvate condenses with oxaloacetate to form citrate
Oxidative phosphorylation occurs in the cytoplasm
Alpha keto glutarate is a 4 carbon compound

questions.correctAnswerText: It is the final common pathway for the oxidation of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins
questions.explanation:
The Krebs cycle is the final common pathway for the oxidation of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins, as glucose, fatty acids, and most amino acids are metabolized to acetyl-CoA or intermediates of the cycle.

Other options:
• Acetyl CoA condenses with oxaloacetate to form citrate.
• Oxidative phosphorylation occurs in mitochondria by the electron transport chain.
• Alpha-ketoglutarate is a 5-carbon compound.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is not an intermediate of the TCA cycle?
questions.explanation:
Acetyl CoA is not an intermediate formed in the TCA cycle, but rather it is a starting substrate.

There are three sources of acetyl-CoA:
• From glucose: pyruvate → acetyl-CoA
• Fatty acid oxidation → acetyl CoA
• Ketogenic amino acid oxidation → acetyl CoA

The starting materials of Krebs cycle are acetyl CoA and oxaloacetic acid. All the other options are intermediates in the TCA cycle, and oxaloacetic acid is released in the end.

The source also depicts the Krebs cycle in a pathway diagram.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Hyperammonemia inhibits the TCA cycle, by depleting levels of which of the following substances?
questions.explanation:
Hyperammonemia results in depletion of alpha-ketoglutarate.

This happens in two steps:
• Excess free ammonia binds to glutamate and forms glutamine.
• To compensate for reduced glutamate, alpha-ketoglutarate is aminated to glutamate.

Thus, hyperammonemia eventually depletes alpha-ketoglutarate, leading to stoppage of the TCA cycle.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Aconitase contains which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Aconitase is a Fe-containing enzyme. It is involved in conversion of citrate to isocitrate.

The process occurs as a two-step reaction catalyzed by aconitase:
• Initial dehydration removes a molecule of water from citrate to form cis-aconitate.
• Rehydration adds a molecule of water to cis-aconitate, thereby forming isocitrate.

Note: Aconitase is involved in iron homeostasis. The source includes a reaction diagram.

questions.question: Which of the following substances inhibits aconitase enzyme?
questions.explanation:
Fluoroacetate is an inhibitor of the aconitase enzyme.

Fluoroacetate combines with Co-A to form fluoroacetyl-CoA. Fluoroacetyl-CoA then condenses with oxaloacetate to form fluorocitrate. Fluorocitrate then inhibits aconitase.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: In the Krebs cycle, which of the following catalyses the step in which the first CO2 is released?
questions.explanation:
Isocitrate dehydrogenase catalyses the step in which the first CO2 is released. CO2 is released and NAD+ is reduced to NADH in this reaction.

There are two oxidative decarboxylation steps in the TCA cycle:
• Isocitrate → alpha-ketoglutarate, catalyzed by isocitrate dehydrogenase.
• Alpha-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA, catalyzed by alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

The source includes a Krebs-cycle pathway diagram.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Substrate level phosphorylation occurs in which of the following steps of the TCA cycle?

options.text: Alpha keto glutarate to succinyl CoA

questions.explanation:
Substrate-level phosphorylation occurs when succinyl CoA is converted to succinate in the TCA cycle.

Succinyl-CoA is converted to succinate by succinate thiokinase, also called succinyl-CoA synthetase. GTP formation takes place in this step; this is the one and only example of substrate-level phosphorylation in the TCA cycle.

The GTP formed is used for decarboxylation of oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate catalyzed by PEPCK in gluconeogenesis. The source includes a Krebs-cycle pathway diagram.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: How many ATPs are generated per turn of the TCA cycle?
questions.explanation:
Total ATP generated per turn of the TCA cycle is 10.

ATP-yielding steps:
• Isocitrate → alpha-ketoglutarate: 1 NADH per turn.
• Alpha-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA: 1 NADH per turn.
• Succinyl CoA → succinate: 1 GTP by substrate-level phosphorylation.
• Succinate → fumarate: 1 FADH2.
• Malate → oxaloacetate: 1 NADH.

Equivalent ATP:
• 3 × NADH = 7.5 ATP
• 1 × FADH2 = 1.5 ATP
• 1 × GTP = 1 ATP
• Total = 10 ATP per turn.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: All of the following serve as cofactors for the enzymes of the TCA cycle, except:
questions.explanation:
Biotin (B7) is not a cofactor for TCA-cycle enzymes.

Vitamins that serve as cofactors for TCA-cycle enzymes:
• Riboflavin (B2): active form FAD; cofactor for succinate dehydrogenase.
• Niacin (B3): active form NAD+; cofactor for isocitrate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and malate dehydrogenase.
• Thiamine (B1): active form thiamine diphosphate; cofactor for the decarboxylation step of alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex.
• Pantothenic acid (B5): active as part of coenzyme A; participates in esterified carboxylic-acid residues such as acetyl-CoA and succinyl-CoA.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Why is the TCA cycle called as an amphibolic pathway?

options.text: Both oxidative and synthetic reactions take place
Metabolites are utilized in other pathways
It can proceed both in forward and backward direction
Same enzymes can be used in reverse direction

questions.correctAnswerText: Both oxidative and synthetic reactions take place
questions.explanation:
In the TCA cycle, both oxidative and synthetic reactions take place.

The TCA cycle is not only a pathway for oxidation but also for interconversion of metabolites arising from transamination and deamination of amino acids. It provides substrates for amino-acid synthesis by transamination as well as for gluconeogenesis and fatty-acid synthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a cofactor of the enzyme alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase?
questions.explanation:
Pyridoxal phosphate is not a cofactor of alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

The alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase enzyme complex has five coenzymes:

• Thiamine pyrophosphate
• NAD+
• FAD
• Coenzyme A

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: All of the following enzymes are components of the pyruvate dehydrogenase enzyme complex, except
questions.explanation:
Pyruvate kinase is not a component of the pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) enzyme complex.

PDH is a multienzyme complex associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane and catalyzes oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA.

The three enzyme components are:
• Pyruvate dehydrogenase
• Dihydrolipoyl transacetylase
• Dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase

The cofactors are:
• Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP)
• Lipoic acid
• Coenzyme A
• FAD
• NAD+

Overall reaction: Pyruvate + NAD+ + CoA → Acetyl-CoA + NADH + H+ + CO2.

Clinical aspects:
• Arsenite and mercuric ions react with -SH groups of lipoic acid and inhibit pyruvate dehydrogenase.
• Dietary thiamine deficiency inhibits PDH; chronic alcoholics may develop potentially fatal pyruvic and lactic acidosis.
• Inherited pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency presents with lactic acidosis, particularly after a glucose load, and neurological disturbances.

Note: Pyruvate kinase catalyzes the last step of glycolysis, transferring phosphate from phosphoenolpyruvate to ADP to form pyruvate and ATP.

• Riboflavin-derived FAD is the cofactor for succinate dehydrogenase, which converts succinate to fumarate.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Identify the anaplerotic reaction among the following?

options.text: Conversion of pyruvate to Acetyl CoA
Conversion of pyruvate to Lactic acid

questions.explanation:
Conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate is an anaplerotic reaction, catalyzed by pyruvate carboxylase.

Anaplerotic reactions form intermediates of a metabolic pathway. This reaction is important in maintaining an adequate concentration of oxaloacetate for condensation with acetyl-CoA. If acetyl-CoA accumulates, it activates pyruvate carboxylase and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase, ensuring an adequate supply of oxaloacetate.

Other anaplerotic reactions:
• Compounds yielding propionyl CoA can be carboxylated and isomerized to succinyl CoA.
• Glutamate and glutamine yield alpha-ketoglutarate via glutaminase and glutamate dehydrogenase reactions.
• Transamination of aspartate leads directly to formation of oxaloacetate.

If acetyl-CoA accumulates, it activates pyruvate carboxylase and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase, ensuring an adequate supply of oxaloacetate.

Other anaplerotic reactions:
• Compounds yielding propionyl CoA can be carboxylated and isomerized to succinyl CoA.
• Glutamate and glutamine yield alpha-ketoglutarate via glutaminase and glutamate dehydrogenase reactions.
• Transamination of aspartate leads directly to formation of oxaloacetate.

blocks.text: Conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate is an anaplerotic reaction, catalyzed by pyruvate carboxylase.

Anaplerotic reactions form intermediates of a metabolic pathway. This reaction is important in maintaining an adequate concentration of oxaloacetate for condensation with acetyl-CoA. If acetyl-CoA accumulates, it activates pyruvate carboxylase and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase, ensuring an adequate supply of oxaloacetate.
